title: What moved the price and what to watch
body:
## A chronology built on governance, not product

POET's price-relevant event log between mid-2024 and the snapshot date reads more like a governance and capital-structure story than a product roadmap. Three board appointments, the retirement of a thirteen-year incumbent, a $250 million institutional equity raise, and a single named strategic collaboration were the primary information events that moved sentiment. Against that backdrop, the company's quarterly 6-K filings produced one consistent signal: a pre-revenue NRE line ticking upward in increments too small to matter commercially but large enough to demonstrate continued customer-engagement activity. Understanding which of those events actually re-rated the equity — and which served mainly as framing — is the analytical task for an investor constructing a forward catalyst map.

## The governance reshaping: December 2024 – July 2025

The most consequential cluster of POET disclosures in the twelve months before the snapshot date was not a technology milestone but a board reconstitution executed in three deliberate instalments across December 2024 through July 2025.

In December 2024, POET announced the appointment of Robert (Bob) Tirva as a director. Tirva arrived at a precise moment: the company had just closed the largest institutional financing in its history and needed a publicly credentialled financial executive to govern the balance sheet through what management characterised as a multi-year qualification runway. His track record — CFO and COO at Sonim Technologies, earlier strategy and finance roles at Broadcom, IBM, and Dropbox — carried Broadcom-side familiarity with the hyperscaler-component supply chain the Optical Interposer was designed to serve.

Six months later, at the June 2025 annual general meeting, Chris Tsiofas retired from the board after thirteen years as a director and Audit Committee Chair. Tsiofas had governed POET across the Venkatesan pivot, the Singapore build-out, and the transition from a Toronto-listed micro-cap to a dual-listed NASDAQ equity. His retirement closed what was effectively the founding-era governance chapter. Tirva — six months in and credentialled for the role — was the natural successor at the audit committee, transferring the financial oversight function from a long-tenure director to one calibrated for the post-financing execution phase.

The July 2025 appointment of Sohail Khan completed the reshaping. Khan's profile was the deepest compound-semiconductor operating credential on the board since Jean-Louis Malinge joined in September 2017 with his Kotura-to-Mellanox CEO track record. Khan had served as EVP at Coherent, as CEO at Agere Systems and ViXS Systems, and had spent sixteen years on the board of LightPath Technologies. Coherent — formerly II-VI — is a vertically integrated photonics manufacturer with InP and silicon photonic components operating in the same supply-chain layer the Optical Interposer targets. Khan's long familiarity with that competitive and partner landscape placed photonics-M&A pattern recognition directly at the governance table.

Taken together, the three-instalment reshaping represented a shift in governance posture: from building platform credibility to governing balance-sheet execution and supply-chain qualification through to a commercial revenue line.

## The $250 million financing: what it meant and what it cost

The single largest re-rating event in POET's 2025 was the close of a $250 million institutional equity financing from three undisclosed institutional buyers. The transaction expanded total assets from $69.7 million at December 2024 to $328.6 million at December 2025 — a nearly fivefold balance-sheet expansion achieved without a commercial revenue line to underwrite it. Cash and short-term investments stood at $313.4 million at year-end, as reported in the [FY2025 fourth-quarter financial results](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-reports-fourth-quarter-2025-financial-results) and confirmed in the 20-F annual report filed in February 2026.

At the FY2025 operating cash burn — net loss of $62.96 million, partially offset by approximately $18 million of non-cash items — the balance sheet implies runway of approximately five to seven years without additional capital. Management's public framing was consistent: the financing provided the capital to execute the Optical Interposer qualification process without requiring a secondary raise in the near term.

But the financing carried a structural cost the equity market is still pricing. The 37.36 million warrants outstanding at the snapshot date — created in part through the transaction — sit alongside 5.79 million options against 132.3 million common shares in issue. Full exercise would dilute existing shareholders by approximately 28.35 percent. The non-cash accounting recognition of that overhang appears on the balance sheet as a $135.6 million derivative warrant liability — mark-to-market, rising as the share price rises, creating a structural headwind precisely when the thesis is working.

| Capital-structure item | Value at Dec 31, 2025 |
|---|---|
| Common shares outstanding | 132.3M |
| Options outstanding | 5.79M |
| Warrants outstanding | 37.36M |
| Implied fully diluted shares | ~175.45M |
| Dilution if fully exercised | ~28.4% |
| Derivative warrant liability | $135.6M |
| Cash + short-term investments | $313.4M |

## Quarterly filing rhythm: a pre-revenue line slowly accumulating

The 6-K quarterly filing cadence across 2024 and 2025 produced one consistent data series: minimal but incrementally growing NRE-and-product receipts against a stable and significant operating loss. Q3 2024 produced $3,685 of revenue. Q4 2024 produced $29,032. Q2 2025 crossed the $250,000 threshold at $268,469. Q3 2025 produced $298,434 and Q4 2025 produced $341,202, as reported in the [Q3 2025 financial results](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-reports-third-quarter-2025-financial-results) and the subsequent fourth-quarter release.

The trajectory is directionally positive but does not constitute commercial revenue. POET's $1.2 million of total FY2025 revenue covers approximately three days of R&D spend at the annualised $18 million rate. The 20-F explicitly acknowledges "limited operating history in the data center market" — a disclosure no investor should overlook. What the NRE receipts do signal is ongoing customer-engagement activity: NRE payments are made for engineering work on specific customer programs, and their incremental growth from Q3 2024 through Q4 2025 suggests the qualification pipeline deepened over the twelve-month period, even without a disclosed named design win.

## The Sivers collaboration: POET's first named strategic partner

In September 2025, POET and Sivers Semiconductors [announced a collaboration](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-and-sivers-semiconductors-collaborate-on-external-light-sources-for-co-packaged-optics-and-next-generation-ai-market) on external light sources for co-packaged optics and the next-generation AI market. The collaboration paired Sivers' UK subsidiary Sivers Photonics — a designer of custom high-power indium phosphide distributed-feedback lasers — with POET's Optical Interposer to produce external light source module candidates for hyperscaler CPO supply chains.

The announcement was the most concrete named strategic partnership POET had disclosed at the snapshot date. Its significance is architectural: co-packaged optics requires a laser source positioned outside the package in the external light source configuration, and the ELS approach is precisely the path the collaboration targeted. The pairing of two pre-revenue platform companies — neither had commercial CPO volume at announcement — at the component layer of a supply chain that itself remained in pre-production across most hyperscaler programs meant the collaboration was a proof-of-reference-design event rather than a revenue catalyst. It demonstrated that a named semiconductor company with its own photonics process capability had chosen the Optical Interposer as the integration platform for its laser products in the CPO context.

## Forward catalysts: what to watch from the snapshot date

Price action in POET from the snapshot date forward is likely to be driven by a small set of binary or near-binary events rather than by quarterly operating leverage.

**Broadcom Tomahawk CPO production ramp.** Broadcom has been the most consequential demand-side validator for CPO at scale. Tomahawk 5 CPO is the reference program against which hyperscalers set their own CPO deployment timelines. Any announcement of volume production commencement or of qualified optical-engine supplier wins in the Tomahawk supply chain would directly re-rate POET's probability of participation. The absence of POET from a named Broadcom CPO announcement is the equal-and-opposite catalyst.

**Nvidia Rubin generation CPO disclosures.** Nvidia's next-generation GPU architecture has been discussed in conjunction with CPO as a potential optical interconnect approach at scale. A concrete Nvidia CPO roadmap announcement — with qualifying architecture requirements, supplier timelines, or volume targets — would materially expand the addressable market for Optical Interposer-based ELS products.

**A qualified design win from POET.** The company characterised its go-to-market as qualifying with hyperscaler programs through OEM/ODM channels and direct engineering teams. The qualification cycle for novel photonic-integration architectures is typically eighteen to thirty-six months from engagement through volume commitment — placing the earliest realistic named design-win announcements in the 2026-to-2027 window from the snapshot date.

**Warrant exercise and the share structure.** Thirty-seven-point-three-six million warrants represent a permanent overhang. If the equity sustains a price above warrant exercise levels — which would require meaningful progress on one of the above catalysts — exercise will expand the share count by up to 28 percent and extinguish the $135.6 million derivative warrant liability. The net NAV impact for existing shareholders depends entirely on the exercise price relative to the market price at exercise.

| Catalyst | Probability horizon | Character |
|---|---|---|
| Broadcom Tomahawk CPO supplier named | 2026 | Binary — named or not |
| Nvidia Rubin CPO roadmap disclosure | 2026–2027 | Binary with scale dimension |
| POET qualified design win | 2026–2027 | Binary |
| Warrant exercise above strike | Contingent on price | Continuous dilution event |
| Additional strategic partnership | 2026–2027 | Incremental validation |

## Specialist-commentary subsection: how price-target chatter framed the move

*Third-party commentary is not used as a primary source elsewhere in this report. This subsection is bounded to 200 words.*

Specialist commentary framing of POET by Aleabit was not surfaced in the bounded primary-source set used for this report. Aleabit's exact published targets or conviction framing — if they exist and are relevant to the 2024-to-2026 price action — were not included in the primary-source materials assembled for this chapter, and are accordingly not cited here as fact.

What primary sources do establish is the general condition set under which specialist commentary tends to catalyse price moves in small-cap pre-revenue photonics equities: a combination of a sudden balance-sheet expansion (the $250 million financing), a named institutional buyer group (three undisclosed institutions), and a named technology collaboration (Sivers, September 2025) creates the conditions for specialist-commentary amplification. That combination was present in POET's 2025 disclosures. Whether Aleabit or the broader photonics-specialist analyst community mapped a specific price target or rating change to those conditions is a question the primary-source set cannot answer at the snapshot date. Investors should weight specialist commentary accordingly: as a framing layer on primary disclosures, not a substitute for reading the 20-F.
